title: Hushfacebook fingerprint signature
description: What scripts/FingerprintCandidates.java captures about one method of a Facebook build, so it can rank the methods of a later build as that method's replacement. Everything here survives a Redex rebuild or is marked as a name that doesn't. The tool writes exactly these properties and refuses a file of another schema or version.

version.description: Bumped when a property's meaning changes. A signature of another version is refused rather than read the new way.

source.description: The build the method was captured from.

sha256.description: The APK's SHA-256. Empty when the signature was captured in memory, as calibration does.

descriptor.description: The method as that build names it, obfuscated names and all. Kept for the report; it is never matched.

classKept.description: False when Redex renamed the class into package X.

nameKept.description: False when the name has the shape Redex gives, an upper-case letter and two more.

prototype.description: Parameter and return types with every obfuscated class written LX;, as (LX;I)J.

strings.description: Every string the method loads, once each.

literals.description: N: a narrow literal of 256 or more, resource ids left out. W: a wide literal. WA: and WB: the two MobileConfig id families with their version and slot bytes masked.

references.description: M: a method call and F: a field access, obfuscated classes written X and obfuscated names ?. T: a kept type the method names. C: a kept class it touches.

context.description: The defining class. K: its name when kept. KR: the name Redex left in its __redex_internal_original_name. KS: its nearest kept superclass. KI: a kept interface. KC: a stable sample of its strings.

opcodes.description: Each instruction's opcode family, in order, with the width suffix taken off (const/4 is const).

count.description: Methods calling this one, directly or through a supertype.

tokens.description: What the first 400 callers hold: their strings (S:), class context tokens, kept names (NM:) and prototypes (PR:).
